head.name: @fzlt/core/arcade
head.lead: The shell every page arcade game repeats, so a game is only its rules and its art. One engine per run over the host page (@fzlt/core/board-page: its words are terrain, its buttons are targets), a fixed overlay with a canvas and a scoreboard in the Board UI kit (title, sound, pause, fold and exit keys, readouts, an optional meter, action keys, a comms toast), keys and pointer (@fzlt/core/input), the touch pad on coarse pointers (@fzlt/core/pad), sound from the event ring (@fzlt/core/sound), sparks and stacking score popups, factory health painted into the buttons, and a controller a hub drives: start, pause, resume, stop, destroy, getSnapshot. While a run is live, a click on the page fires instead of following a link; the scoreboard, fields and [data-virus-ignore] / [data-fizlet-ignore] keep their clicks. Recall (Escape, the exit key, stop) destroys the engine, so every letter and button comes back exactly; a run that ends keeps the scoreboard with the result until Recall. The game supplies create(ctx): its own systems on ctx.engine, reading ctx.ctl (written in the read phase) and drawing in render. The scoreboard and controls are a HUD preset, chosen per game with hud (BOARD-UI.md §19): arcadeHud() is today's card and the default (no hud renders it byte for byte); skirmishHud({...}) is Battlefield Blitz's top bar with a clock, rank and armor bar, a feed, a banner, aim toggles and counted keys, and its flow (countdown, pause / surrender, result) on @fzlt/core/match: then match owns the phase, the shell asks it to pause, resume or end and follows it (HudView.ask, HudRun.go). Each preset is its own export, so a game ships only the one it names.

sizesNote: Measured on this build: minified and gzipped with everything it imports, the way npm run size checks the budget in CI.
